Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire
devices using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings
are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818)
548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City
Clerk's Office. For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public
comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed. If you have
any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the City Clerk
at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.
Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.

5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Councilmember Brotman said the he wanted to wish everyone a Happy Chinese New Year,
  but this happy occasion has been marred by the mass shootings in Monterey Park and Half
  Moon Bay and his heart goes out to the families of the victims.

  Brotman attended a training of trainers session organized by Glendale CERT and Sparr
  Heights Connect and Prepare called “Map your Neighborhood.” The goal was to provide a
  tool that would help neighborhoods be better prepared for disasters. In addition to the

  2
 training, Councilmembers had the opportunity to hear a presentation by Glendale resident
Isabel Myer, who has extensive experience and knowledge of this topic. The Council also
heard from representatives of the Santa Monica Mountain Resource Conservation District
who spoke about how to make homes more fire resistant and how to access resources that
are free to the public including wildfire home evaluation, defensible space landscape
designs, community trading training and others. Brotman asked staff to provide a report on
how to bring these trainings and resources to the larger Glendale community. Asatryan
seconded.

Brotman stated that he would like to see how the building electrification ordinance can be
extended to major remodels and how the city can support retrofits of the existing building
stock. He indicated that there’s a lot of funds in the Inflation Reduction Act and he would like
the funds to be used for a program for residents doing major remodels to swap-out gas
appliances for electric ones. Asatryan asked if the request can be clarified, and City
Manager Golanian stated the existing ordinance covers new construction and there is no
demarcation line as to what percentage of remodeling constitutes a requirement to have
electric appliances. Brotman stated that he would like to have a discussion with Council to
clarify what constitutes a major remodel. Asatryan seconded.

Councilmember Najarian indicated that although it is great to have new proposals presented
to Council, he wants to make sure that it does not jump over long-standing requests he
made. City Manager Roubik Golanian indicate that there will be an upcoming City Council
workshop and one of the items for discussion is to have an equitable system for addressing
requests from councilmembers.

Councilmember Asatryan relayed her condolences and words of support to those impacted
by the tragedy in Monterey Park. She stated that “regardless of where acts of violence occur
it rocks all of us.” Asatryan would like to have the City launch a continuous campaign that
would inform the public about mental health services available for community members.
Asatryan thanked the Police and Fire Chiefs and City Manager Golanian for reaching out to
the City of Monterey Park to offer support.

Councilmember Devine joined her colleagues in sending her condolences to the families of
the victims of the Monterey Park shooting. She asked members of the public to reach out to
anyone who they know, who has anger issues or mental health issues, to get them the help
that they need. Additionally, she spoke about the need for stronger gun control legislation.
She also thanked Public Works staff for all they did during the recent rain storms.

Councilmember Najarian also offered his condolences for the families of the victims of the
Monterey Park shooting. He stated that the shooter at Monterey Park had been in contact
with law enforcement for some time and they were aware that he had been displaying signs
of mental instability. He wondered what more could have been done to address his mental
health issues. He asked that the City of Glendale take a more proactive approach for these
types of scenarios and do welfare checks and whatever it takes to prevent such mass
shootings from happening - keeping in mind that this is a complex issue with no simple
solution.

Mayor Kassakhian echoed his colleagues and their comments regarding the tragedy that
happened in the City of Monterey Park and extend his condolences to the families of the
victims and to the residents of the communities who have been rocked by this senseless act
of violence. Kassakhian made a call for people to come together across partisan lines to try

  3
   and find a common solution. He stated that preventing these sorts of tragedies is not just
  about gun laws, legislation, and universal background checks but also about mental health.
  He asked staff to look into bringing back the “Gun Buy Back Program” and other programs
  that turn donated guns into other objects like garden tools. Asatryan second.
